test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Indian languages were given the status of classical languages of India in October 2024?

options.text: Malayalam, Odia, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
Marathi, Odia, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
Marathi, Malayalam, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali

solution:
The correct answer is __**Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In October 2024, the Government of India granted classical language status to five Indian languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali.
 
• This recognition aims to highlight and preserve the rich cultural and linguistic heritage associated with these languages.
 
• Classical language status provides certain benefits, including financial assistance for the development of the language, and academic research and funding for translation projects.
 
• Only languages with a rich heritage and history of more than 1500-2000 years are considered for classical status by the Government of India.
 
• The announcement was made by the Ministry of Culture, which oversees the promotion and protection of Indian languages and cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Languages of India:**

 
 
• As of 2024, India recognizes 11 classical languages, including Tamil, Sanskrit, Kannada, Telugu, Malayalam, Odia, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali. 
 
• The criteria for classical language status include a significant body of ancient literature, a long history, and an original tradition.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Classical Language Status:**
 
 
• Classical languages receive financial support for setting up centers of excellence for study and research.
 
• The status facilitates the translation of classical texts into other Indian languages and English.
 
 
 
• **Pali and Prakrit:**
 
 
• Pali is an ancient language, primarily used in the Theravada Buddhist scriptures.
 
• Prakrit refers to a group of middle Indo-Aryan languages that were spoken in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Assamese and Bengali:**
 
 
• Assamese is the easternmost Indo-Aryan language, spoken mainly in the state of Assam.
 
• Bengali is the second most spoken language in India and has a rich literary heritage, including works by Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
